title: Tiple (Colombian twelve-string guitar)
summary: The tiple is a small Colombian guitar with twelve strings in four courses of three. The triple strings ring together and give it a bright, shimmering voice. It is strummed and plucked in dances and songs, often beside the bandola and a larger guitar.
howToPlay: Four courses of strings run down the neck, the lowest on the left. Each lane marks the fret where a note is played.
A bead slides down the strings to its fret. Pluck the lane as the bead lands.
The wide lanes over the sound hole are strums: tap one to sound a whole chord.
Try the bambuco sway first, then the bright pairs, then the gentle arc.
rules: The notes come from a scale starting on D, with chords on D minor and G minor.
Every phrase is played through twice.
A pluck or strum on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
The bambuco sway counts six beats to the bar; the others count four.
heritageNote: The tiple belongs to the song and dance music of the Colombian highlands. Makers glue and brace the slim body by hand, and the three strings of each course are tuned together so that they shimmer when strummed.
